title: Regional prefetch starvation causing token-rate drop — customer escalations across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Summary: Multiple customers in NA and EU reported TTFT regressions and drop in tokens/sec beginning 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC. Impact spans Hosted API, Dedicated pools (region us-east-1), and several Private VPC deployments that use the prefetch+KV cache path. Symptoms: elevated first-token latency (TTFT), reduced sustained tokens/sec per worker, and increased cold KV fetches. Root cause (hypothesis): a prefetch heuristic change rolled in runtime-1.21 (kernel selector refinements) overaggressively demoted certain model fanout requests from 'opportunistic prefetch' to 'deferred prefetch', causing KV cache eviction pressure in high-fanout regional bursts -> increased disk/remote reads -> TTFT and throughput reductions. Goal: restore baseline TTFT and tokens/sec for affected customers within 24–48h while shipping a safe, reversible hotfix.
impact_details: Reported by 4 enterprise customers (priority accounts), multiple internal alerting signals: 30% increase in TTFT P95 on us-east-1, 20–40% decline in tokens/sec on dedicated pools between 22:00–02:00 UTC. Private deployments show similar pattern when traffic is unevenly fanout-heavy. No data corruption. Major impact to interactive product SLAs; some customers opened urgent escalations with CSMs.
root_cause_analysis: Initial triage: correlated TTFT spikes with increased KV-miss rate and longer disk read latencies. Kernel/fallback telemetry shows higher frequency of the 'deferred prefetch' code path. A recent heuristic (commit c3f4b2) attempts to avoid redundant prefetch during short-lived sessions but mis-classifies multi-model prompt fanout as 'short', leading to insufficient KV population. Secondary effect: eviction churn where hot prefixes are evicted due to sudden fanout bursts. Not a hardware failure; deterministic under certain request fanout/seq distributions.
mitigation_plan: 1) Immediate: deploy 'prefetch circuit-breaker' toggle to force 'opportunistic prefetch' for affected pools/regions (hotfix flag) and increase per-worker KV cache window from 2s -> 6s to reduce eviction churn. 2) Short-term (24–72h): roll kernel selector rollback for specific heuristic (revert commit c3f4b2) in runtime-1.22-hotfix branch. 3) Medium-term: add telemetry guardrails and a classifier to detect 'multi-model fanout' and apply conservative prefetch. 4) Postmortem: design durable mitigation in runtime-1.23 with tests and regression suite.
deployment_plan: Stage 1: toggle flag via runtime feature-gateway for hosted and dedicated region us-east-1 (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%, target completion within 2 hours). Stage 2: apply the same toggle to Private control-plane manifests customers that opt-in via support-runbook. Stage 3: merge rollback commit to hotfix branch and publish runtime-1.22.1 (canary + smoke tests) then roll to all Dedicated pools. Rollback: revert flag and promote previous runtime if metrics worsen.
tests_and_validation: - Canary charts: TTFT P50/P95, tokens/sec per worker, KV miss rate, disk read latency. - Run synthetic multi-model fanout workload against canary cluster with load-tool v2 (script: tools/fanout_synth.sh). - Smoke tests: sample customer prompt sets (links below). - Acceptance: restore TTFT P95 to within 5% of baseline and tokens/sec to within 10%.
communication_plan: - Inform affected CSMs and customers with an ETA 30m after canary start. - Post daily updates to #incident-runtime and support@redwood. - Prepare customer-facing postmortem summarizing root cause and timeline.
